title: Bouncing Light
description: You found the first shard of the Rainbow Crystal — but it's trapped behind Umbra's mirror maze. To pass, you must learn how light bounces: the science of reflection.

content.value: When light hits a surface and bounces back, we call it REFLECTION. A smooth, shiny surface like a mirror reflects light so well that you can see a clear image in it.
To describe reflection exactly, scientists use four key terms. Learn them now — you'll use them in every mirror mission.

INCIDENT RAY   → the ray of light going TOWARD the mirror
REFLECTED RAY  → the ray that BOUNCES back off the mirror
NORMAL         → an imaginary line at 90° to the mirror, at the point of hit
POINT OF INCIDENCE → the exact spot where light strikes the mirror

incident \   | normal   / reflected
   ray       \  |         /  ray
              \ |  angles /
 ______________\|________/______________  ← mirror surface
The NORMAL is not a real line you can see — it is a helper line drawn at 90° to the mirror. All reflection angles are measured from the normal, NOT from the mirror surface.
Key Takeaway: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface. The incoming ray is the incident ray, the bounced ray is the reflected ray, and both angles are measured from the normal.

quiz.question: The ray of light that travels toward the mirror is called the…
quiz.explain: The incident ray is the incoming ray. After it bounces off, it becomes the reflected ray.

quiz.question: What is the 'normal' in reflection?
options: The shiniest part of the mirror
An imaginary line drawn at 90° to the mirror at the point of incidence
quiz.explain: The normal is a helper line at right angles (90°) to the mirror. We measure the angles of reflection from it.

quiz.question: Angles in reflection are measured from the…
quiz.explain: Both the angle of incidence and angle of reflection are always measured from the normal, not the mirror surface.
